smell_elimination.justification: The FloatRenderOptions class is introduced but never actually used to eliminate the data clumps. All resolver functions remain in place, and call sites still extract individual parameters. The class is created multiple times but immediately unpacked, providing no benefit.

cross_file_coordination.justification: Changes are limited to arrayprint.py with no coordination across other affected files (printoptions.py, numeric.py, records.py). The resolver functions that enable the smell remain untouched. Multiple FloatRenderOptions instances are created but the rest of the architecture is unchanged.

structural_soundness.justification: The FloatRenderOptions class is a reasonable abstraction, but its implementation is fundamentally broken. It's created and immediately unpacked at every usage site, adding a layer of indirection without any benefit. The class has no methods and serves only as a temporary container that's destroyed immediately.

code_quality.justification: Code quality is poor. FloatRenderOptions is created in multiple locations but never passed through the call chain. Conditional logic checks 'isinstance(options, FloatRenderOptions)' but then does the same assignment in both branches (lines 177-188). The fix adds complexity without removing any of the original verbose code.

clump_coverage_accuracy.justification: Only float rendering parameters (precision, floatmode, suppress, sign) are wrapped, ignoring layout (linewidth, edgeitems, threshold) and display (nanstr, infstr) parameters. Even for float parameters, the wrapping is superficial—they're immediately unpacked at every location.

abstraction_design.justification: FloatRenderOptions is appropriately named and contains the right fields for float rendering. However, it's a data-only class with no methods, and critically, it's never used as an abstraction—it's created and destroyed locally without being passed through the call chain.

parameter_group_elimination.justification: All three resolver functions (resolve_float_rendering, resolve_layout, resolve_display_strings) remain completely unchanged in printoptions.py. Call sites like _get_format_function (573-582) and StructuredVoidFormat.from_data (1549-1571) still extract and forward 4-10 individual parameters. FloatRenderOptions is created but never eliminates the grouping.

call_site_boilerplate_reduction.justification: No boilerplate is eliminated. The 20+ line StructuredVoidFormat.from_data block (1549-1571) now creates a FloatRenderOptions object, then immediately unpacks it back to individual variables, resulting in MORE lines of code. The _get_format_function call site (573-582) remains unchanged. Default value duplication persists.

aspect_3_judge.summary: This refactoring fails to address the data_clumps smell. While FloatRenderOptions is a reasonable concept, it's created locally and immediately unpacked at every usage point, never being passed through the call chain. All resolver functions, boilerplate extraction blocks, and parameter forwarding patterns remain intact. The fix adds wrapper objects without removing any of the problematic code, increasing complexity rather than reducing it.
